title: Chapter 38: The Meaning of Courage
content:
Chapter 38:

The Meaning of Courage

He dashed out of the room, sprinted down the hallway, and bounded down the stairs.

Skipping three steps at a time, he landed on the landing, immediately spun around and leapt again. The moment his feet hit the first floor, he threw his head back and—

“—Ram! Rem! We need to talk!”

Shouting loud enough for the whole mansion to hear, Subaru made a beeline for the entrance hall.

He looked ready to burst right out the front door without slowing down. What stopped him in his tracks was the sight of Ram, who had beaten him to the entrance.

It probably wasn’t so much that she had anticipated his move, but simply that she happened to be closer. It also meant she had more time on her hands than Rem, who was busy prepping a meal in the kitchen.

Seeing something in Subaru’s blood-pumping, frantic expression, Ram let a hint of surprise slip through her usually composed features.

“What’s wrong, Barusu? You’re in such a panic…”

“Sorry, but I’m heading to the village. There’s no point trying to stop me, and I’m going even if you do, but I figured leaving without a word would just cause a panic.”

“To the village…? For what…? No, before that, did you completely ignore Master Roswaal’s instructions? Tonight, Ram and the others have been entrusted with the mansion. Are you saying you don’t understand what that means?”

Ram’s glare grew sharper as she shot back at him.

Above all else, her stance was to prioritize Roswaal’s will. Subaru’s blatant disregard for their master’s orders had clearly struck a nerve.

However, Subaru wasn’t in any state of mind to just back down, either.

“I don’t have time to stand here arguing, so I’ll give it to you straight. —There’s an evil magician in that village. I figured out who it is, so I have to go.”

“…And you expect Ram to accept an excuse that sounds like a child made it up?”

“It’s the only way I can explain it, so deal with it. If you want proof it’s the truth, go ask Beako, she’ll back me up. Other than that…”

“Sister—”

While he was trying to defend himself to an increasingly suspicious Ram, the heavy doors behind them opened, and Rem appeared. Catching sight of the two bickering in the entryway, she glided over to stand beside her sister.

“Sister, what is…?”

“He says he’s off to defeat an evil magician in the village, so we need to let him out. —Whatever shall we do, Rem?”

Hearing her sister’s blunt summary of the situation, the younger twin blinked in surprise.

Then, as if fully digesting the words, she turned a highly skeptical gaze toward Subaru.

“Sister, Sister. It seems Subaru makes rather terribly boring jokes.”

“Rem, Rem. Barusu is saying things that prove his talents as a clown are truly first-rate.”

“Ram, Rem. I know I usually joke around, but sometimes I’m dead serious.”

Subaru’s quick retort overlapping their synchronized routine made both of them falter in unison.

Capitalizing on their reaction, he took a step forward.

“I admit it sounds completely unbelievable, and I know it’s a lot to ask you to trust me when I’m suddenly running off like this. So I’m not asking you to just wave me off with no questions asked.”

This was where it became a critical crossroads for Subaru.

He wet his lips and made a proposal to the two silent maids, pointing a finger at them.

“I’m heading to the village right now. If you’re suspicious, you’re welcome to come along. See for yourselves. But we can’t leave Emilia-tan here by herself. If you’re coming, only one of you goes.”

“Arbitrarily taking charge… To begin with, if we are to follow Master Roswaal’s orders, there is no reason for Rem or Sister to accompany you…”

“Yeah, none at all. If we’re strictly talking about Ros-chi’s orders from this evening, that is. But are those the only orders Ros-chi gave you regarding me?”

“————”

Rem was left momentarily speechless, as if he’d struck a nerve.

His bluff had apparently hit the bullseye.

The two of them were under orders from Roswaal to keep him under surveillance. It was something he’d already pieced together from fragments of information gathered across his previous loops.

Rem’s eyes continued to dart around as she searched for a rebuttal, but it was Ram who cut through the tension with a soft sigh.

She raised a hand slightly.

“Understood, Barusu. Ram will permit your independent action.”

“Sister—?!”

Rem looked aghast at her sister so readily raising the white flag. But Ram turned her raised palm toward her younger sister and added, “However.”

“As Barusu already knows, we cannot let him go alone. Permitting Barusu to wander off by himself right now would be a violation of Master Roswaal’s orders.”

“Right. So, what’s the compromise?”

“—Galling as it is, but we have no choice but to accept Barusu’s proposal from earlier. Ram will remain at the mansion. Rem will accompany Barusu. If he tries anything suspicious… that is the condition.”

“Exactly what I was hoping for.”

He threw a fist in the air, signaling his agreement to Ram’s terms.

Letting out a small sigh, Ram turned to her younger sister, who had been left somewhat behind in the conversation.

“Rem, that’s how it is, so please take care of it. Ram will handle checking with Lady Beatrice and protecting Lady Emilia. —And I will be keeping a very close eye on things on your end, too.”

“Sister, you shouldn’t use those eyes too much…”

“Now is not the time to worry about that. If it’s necessary, Ram will use them. You do the same, Rem.”

Faced with her sister’s matter-of-fact tone, Rem couldn’t argue any further.

Following an exchange that only the two of them fully understood, Rem swallowed back whatever else she wanted to say and leveled a decidedly unfriendly glare at Subaru.

“Subaru, Rem would like to hear the details of this.”

“On the way. Because it’s entirely possible a seriously bad situation is unfolding right now.”

If Subaru’s worst-case scenario proved right, the fallout could be disastrous enough that nobody would be laughing it off as an exaggeration. And it wouldn’t just be damage to Subaru personally, but damage on a much larger scale.

He gave Ram a light tap on the shoulder as a gesture of thanks for letting him pass.

Then, with a still-unconvinced Rem in tow, he made for the front doors.

Just then,

“—Subaru, are you going somewhere?”

A voice like a silver bell chimed from the top of the grand staircase in the entrance hall.

Glancing up instinctively, he saw Emilia standing there, her silver hair swaying. Subaru’s loud shouting earlier had clearly reached her ears, too.

Slightly breathless, she looked down at the three of them frozen in the entryway.

“I heard a loud voice, so I came down to check… Did something happen?”

“Something might be happening, Emilia-tan. Well, you don’t need to worry about it. Oh, but I wouldn’t mind if you worried just a little bit.”

Subaru deliberately acted like his usual self so as not to cause Emilia any unnecessary anxiety.

Yet, despite Subaru’s unchanging flippant demeanor, Emilia must have noticed something, because—

“You’ve got that look on your face again. Like you’re about to do something dangerous.”

Seeing right through him instantly, Emilia gave him a reproachful look. Scratching his head at her sharp intuition, Subaru tilted his head, wondering how to play it.

“We actually just barely finished arguing over that exact thing…”

“It’s no use trying to stop you, is there?”

“Well, pretty much. In fact, if you did stop me, it’d cause problems on a lot of fronts…”

“Yes, yes, I get it. I won’t try to stop you.”

Emilia descended the stairs, coming to a stop right in front of them with her hands on her hips.

Being stared at straight on by those amethyst eyes, Subaru found himself unable to look away, as if being pulled into their brilliance.

She reached a hand out toward the paralyzed Subaru and rested it lightly against his chest.

“I’d tell you not to overdo it or do anything reckless, but that seems pointless too, doesn’t it?”

“Depending on the situation… yeah. Honestly, I don’t want to do any of that either.”

Effort, hard work, desperation—words like that were all things he’d rather avoid.

Even so, when he was the only one who could change the situation, Subaru had no choice but to act. Why had he developed such a troublesome disposition? He couldn’t help but chuckle wryly, figuring the girl standing right in front of him had a lot to do with it.

“—May the blessing of the spirits be with you.”

“Come again?”

Subaru tilted his head at the murmur while her hand was still against his chest. At that, Emilia gave him a soft smile.

“It’s a send-off. It just means, ‘please come back safe.’”

“Ah, kinda like striking sparks with a flint for good luck, huh? Then I gotta answer in kind. Emilia-tan, the glory of victory to 

you—”

1

“Yes, yes.”

Brushing off Subaru’s impromptu salute, Emilia turned her gaze to Rem. Rem, who had been watching their exchange in silence, straightened her posture under Emilia’s look.

“Be careful out there, Rem. And keep a close eye on Subaru so he doesn’t do anything reckless.”

“Yes, Lady Emilia. Understood.”

“Zero trust for me, huh.”

“What are you talking about? It’s precisely because I trust the kind of person you are that we’re even having this conversation.”

“What kind of trust is that? It could be taken as a good thing or a bad thing—talk about demonically possessed.”

Emilia still had her hands on her hips, firmly in lecture mode.

She undoubtedly had plenty more she wanted to say, but that was as far as she pushed it. Understanding Subaru’s urgency, she gave his back a gentle shove.

“Have a safe trip.”

“Aye, I’m off!”

Spurred by the push, he responded by thrusting his fist up, bolting out of the mansion and leaving Emilia and Ram behind. Rem bowed before exiting the mansion, following after him, and he soon sensed her effortlessly pulling up alongside him as he ran.

“So, Rem would like to hear those details now…”

“There’s a curse arts user in the village. Beatrice broke the curse for me, but I’d already been cursed myself. —If things go south, the whole village might be wiped out.”

“—Are you serious?”

Running beside him, Rem gasped and asked the question with her eyes wide.

Subaru answered with a silent nod, his focus entirely on reaching the village.

If the curse arts user were a rational human being, there’d be no need to imagine such extreme measures. But if Subaru’s theory proved correct, the worst-case scenario was a very real possibility.

Therefore, Subaru pushed himself to run faster. Running beside him, Rem, too, now grasped the gravity of the situation and sprinted in silence.

Aiming for the village far off beyond the trees, the two figures tore through the night’s darkness.

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

“—Subaru, that’s…”

Subaru heard Rem call out, her voice brimming with palpable tension.

Rem, raising her voice, was already quite a bit ahead of his line of sight. She was pointing toward the village, its outline now coming into clear view, and the look on her face said it all.

“The village is awfully bright…”

Coming to the exact same conclusion, Subaru also sensed the signs of something terribly wrong.

His steps grew heavy; his all-out sprint had dropped to a pace too slow to be called running, but too fast to be called walking.

Unable to suppress her urgency, Rem cast an impatient glance at Subaru, but even with her silently prodding him, he had a stitch in his side and couldn’t even manage a shout.

“Go on ahead, go…”

He gestured with his hand for her to lead the way, but Rem shook her head.

To begin with, the reason for her accompanying Subaru was exactly that. She was there to keep an eye on him, so splitting up now would completely defeat the purpose.

Perhaps losing patience with Subaru’s rather pathetic display,

“Fine, it can’t be helped. Please don’t bite your tongue.”

“Eh, wait, Rem-rin, what are you—?!”

Dashing back to Subaru’s side, Rem reached out her arm, grabbed the exhausted Subaru by the scruff of the neck, and hoisted him up effortlessly.

It was an overwhelming display of the difference in their physical strength, much like what she’d shown off with the wine barrels earlier.

Slung over Rem’s shoulder just like that, Subaru’s upside-down body rode the wind.

Experiencing the speed of Rem’s full-out sprint firsthand, Subaru was utterly speechless at her sheer physical prowess. At the same time, it cemented his conviction that bringing her along had been the right call.

What could a powerless, incompetent guy like Subaru possibly hope to accomplish diving into the thick of things all by himself? Including the bluffing back at the entrance, securing a combat asset like Rem had definitely been the right move.

“We’ve arrived. Are you alright, Subaru?”

“Fast, as expected… now we just need to check on the village… blerghhh.”

Resting his hand on the fence, Subaru fought back a wave of nausea brought on by the exhaustion and the bumpy ride.

Ignoring his unseemly state, Rem surveyed the area. Their prominent arrival caught the attention of a villager who happened to be passing by.

“If it isn’t the two from the mansion. At an hour like this…”

“Perfect timing. Has something happened?”

Catching the young man as he jogged over, Rem interrogated him from above. He widened his eyes, slightly startled by her forceful tone, and replied with a cracked voice, “Y-Yes.”

“Actually, some of the village children have gone missing. We know they were playing until just before it got dark, but after that…”

At the young man’s vague explanation, Rem opened her mouth to press him further.

But Subaru beat her to it. Still panting heavily, he placed a hand on the young man’s shoulder, making him turn around.

“The missing ones, is it Lucas, Petra, and Mild?”

“Y-Yes, that’s right… do you have any idea where they might have gone?”

Receiving the answer that confirmed his fears, Subaru clicked his tongue and kicked the dirt, swearing, “Dammit!” He then locked his gaze on the outskirts of the village—toward the fence that led to the forest.

“Who’s searching for the kids, you and who else?”

“The youth group in full force, and the village chief.”

“The kids are in the forest. You won’t find them by scouring the village.”

The young man’s expression changed at Subaru’s absolute certainty. He clearly had more questions he wanted to ask, but Subaru patted his shoulder and took off running.

“I’m heading into the forest first. Tell the others. The kids are in the forest!”

Behind him, the young man called out in confusion, but Subaru ignored him and broke into a run once more.

Rem hurriedly followed. She couldn’t wrap her head around his total conviction.

“How could you possibly know that…?”

“I just do. Because I’ve heard them say two times now that they found it crying all alone deep in the forest—”

The village was surrounded by a tall wooden fence. Vaulting over the section of the wall bordering the woods, the two of them touched down on the dirt floor of the forest.

They wove through the gaps between the trees, pressing deeper while keeping an eye out for low branches and muddy ground.

“Even if you say they’re in the forest, the area is simply too large. Subaru, do you have any leads…?”

“If what the brats said is true, it should be this way…”

He pushed forward relying on his memory, but his steps were heavy since he was only tracing what he’d been told. To make matters worse, it was pitch black, making it impossible to confirm if he was even going the right way.

However,

“—The barrier is down.”

At Rem’s shocked gasp, Subaru clenched his fist, knowing his intuition had been right.

Right in front of them, Rem was pointing at a crystal embedded in a massive tree. It looked as if it had long since lost its light—it was a mysterious object he’d seen on several occasions in the forest.

He recalled instances where the forest and the barrier had been brought up. When was it that Ram had directly warned him not to go deep into the mountains?

“What happens if the barrier is down?”

“The ‘witchbeasts’ will cross the boundary line. That’s exactly why checking the barrier’s upkeep is a duty of the villagers…!”

“No use dwelling on that, what’s right in front of us is the reality. More importantly, what’s a witchbeast?”

Still shaken, Rem answered Subaru’s question.

“Witchbeasts are… enemies of mankind that possess magical force. To bring ruin to humanity, the Witch created them... so it is told.”

“The Witch again, huh…”

Subaru grimaced at the frequent appearance of a word he couldn’t just gloss over, but the first half of Rem’s explanation confirmed his theory. The true identity of the curse arts user, and the harbinger of the disaster currently threatening the village.

“—! Subaru, what are you doing?!”

Rem cried out in shock, trying to stop him.

Right in front of her, Subaru was crossing past the tree holding the so-called barrier, heading deeper in. Turning back to her surprised face, Subaru held out his left hand.

“The brats are further in. We have to go save them.”

“Do you have any proof of that? Crossing the barrier requires Master Roswaal’s permission…”

“The scar on the back of my hand is all the proof I need.”

He pointed to the back of his left hand—to the bite mark he’d gotten when he visited the village earlier that day.

The teeth marks left by the little dog that had surrounded the children, and which had bestowed its baptism upon Subaru as well.

—Pointing to this exact wound, Beatrice had told him.

The one who gave him this scar was the very same one who cursed him.

The first time, the second time, and now.

The entity involved in every single instance where a curse had fallen upon Subaru. And the very same thing that possessed the potential to claim Rem’s life in this fourth loop.

The only thing that tied every single possibility together was that creature. There was no other explanation.

“It’s the dog the brats were playing with. What if that dog-like thing isn’t actually a dog, and has just been cursing each and every person it bit?”

It wasn’t an artificial act, but more like a natural disaster.

Just like epidemics spread by rats, if it were to spread explosively through an animal, it was easy to imagine what would happen to a single village like this.

And the safety of the children who had chased that dog into the forest was likely in exactly the same peril.

“The longer we take, the worse it gets. I don’t know if the brats have been cursed or not, but either way, we need to drag them all back to the mansion and get them cleansed.”

“Please wait. You can’t just make a decision like that on your own—to begin with, this entire situation is far too suspicious.”

“Huh?”

As an impatient Subaru tried to press into the woods, Rem persistently refused to back down. Pointing back toward the village, and by extension the mansion, she said,

“Would a crisis like this occur so conveniently when Master Roswaal is away? For this not to be a targeted attack on the mansion…”

“Then what do you want to do? Abandon the brats who are without a doubt in immediate, life-threatening danger, and run back to fortify the mansion? If you’re fine with waking up tomorrow to find every last villager dead, then yeah, that’s certainly an option.”

Subaru said it fully aware of how incredibly unfair and cowardly his own argument was.

Rem was merely trying to avoid unnecessary risk. It was a perfectly reasonable reaction, and she didn’t deserve to be blamed for it in the slightest.

However, no matter if they stayed silent or cowered, the time to make a decision would inevitably come.

No matter how limited the options, they had to choose one of the cards dealt to them. Of course, they could also choose to make no choice at all. But the agonizing regret that followed making that particular choice was something still burned deeply, profoundly into the depths of Subaru’s soul.

“Rem, let’s go. It has to be us. We have to do something about this.”

“Why go to such lengths…? How much could this village possibly mean to you…?”

Perhaps still torn over the decision, she muttered the words with a timidity Subaru had never heard from her before. Rem, who had never let her perfectly composed demeanor slip, no matter the situation.

Yet, forced to make a critical call without her trusted lord or her sister present, she reverted to looking like the fragile, age-appropriate girl she really was.

Subaru felt a painfully sharp sense of empathy for that human weakness. But the two of them didn’t have the luxury of standing around licking each other’s wounds right now.

They were out of time, and out of mental bandwidth.

Even as he urged Rem into action, Subaru couldn’t hide the fact that his legs were shaking for reasons entirely unrelated to fatigue. Obviously. He knew that lying in wait up ahead was the very entity that had claimed his life twice, and Rem’s life once.

Much less his companion, his strongest fighting force, not exactly being eager to head deeper. Factoring in the very real possibility that he might have to head into the depths all by himself, how could he possibly keep the cowardice he’d tried so hard to bury from rearing its ugly head?

Still, Subaru slapped his own cheeks, forcing himself to forget that weakness.

The sharp, dry smack made Rem look up. Meeting her gaze, Subaru took a deep breath and spoke in a low voice.

“—Petra wants to move to the capital and make clothes when she grows up.”

“…Eh?”

“Lucas says he’s gonna take over for his dad, the best lumberjack in the village, and Mild wants to make a flower crown from the flowers in the field to give to his mom.”

“…”

Ticking them off on his fingers, Subaru continued, picturing each of their faces behind his eyelids.

“Meina was so happy about having a new little brother or sister soon, and those brothers, Dyne and Cain, are constantly fighting over which one of them is going to marry Petra.”

A small laugh unintentionally escaped his lips.

Then, shaking his head at the silent Rem, he said,

“How could they mean nothing to me? I know their faces, their names, and exactly what they want to do tomorrow.”

Subaru hated kids.

They were loud, overly familiar, talked back to him, and above all, had zero manners.

They were ill-mannered, impolite, reckless, and completely unreserved—like looking in a mirror.

Subaru was far from being an inherently good person.

He was callous enough that even if he saw news of some gruesome tragedy on TV, no matter how appallingly huge the casualty numbers on the screen were, as long as it didn’t hit close to home, he’d forget all about it after a night’s sleep.

That’s why he disliked them, and he wouldn’t care what happened to kids who meant nothing to him.

Honestly, just like Rem said, prioritizing Emilia and the others and holing up in the mansion felt like a much more “Subaru” thing to do. He thought so himself.

But,

“I promised them we’d do radio calisthenics again tomorrow.”

Even during the loop on his first day in this world, Subaru must have felt the exact same way.

Walking out on it all would be so easy. But because he couldn’t, he had run.

He looked at Rem.

She was hesitating over her decision. She was bewildered.

It was a feeble sight. The sight of someone lamenting their own lack of strength. It was the spitting image of Subaru himself.

Seeing her look weaker than he was right now, he felt sick at himself for finally managing to steel his resolve.

The fact that he was terrified and trembling, yet ultimately still trying to use someone else to prop himself up—that utter pettiness filled him with genuine self-loathing.

But if he could use even his own cowardice to his advantage, he would do just that.

“I keep my promises, and I make sure others keep theirs. —I am absolutely doing radio calisthenics with those brats again. That’s why I’m going in.”

—He never knew courage could be this terrifying.

So desperately focused on keeping his shaking hands steady, Subaru delivered his declaration completely oblivious to the tremor in his voice.

Watching Subaru’s back, Rem quietly closed her eyes.

If she wouldn’t come with him, he figured there was nothing he could do about it. Going back now to rally the villagers would be too huge a loss of time. At the very least, he wanted to leave her with instructions to do that, but—

“It simply can’t be helped, can it?”

“Rem?”

Breaking into a small smile, Rem looked up at Subaru.

For what felt like the very first time, she directed an expression bearing clear, distinct emotion toward a surprised Subaru.

“Rem’s ordered duty is to monitor you, Subaru. If Rem were to let you go on alone from here, she would be failing in her duties, wouldn’t she?”

Subaru stared blankly at her teasing words for a moment, then shook his head.

“Yeah, you’re right. Better keep a close eye on me so I don’t try anything suspicious.”

“Yes, Rem will do just that. —So, shall we go?”

As Rem glided over to stand beside him, Subaru straightened his posture, feeling as if he had finally, truly managed to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with her.

A ticklish sort of feeling bubbling up inside him, he was just about to thank her when he suddenly noticed something.

—Before he knew it, Rem had a spiked iron ball in her hand as she walked next to him. Connected to an iron handle by a chain, it let out a light, metallic clinking sound in her grip that completely belied its massive weight.

“Umm, Rem-san, what exactly is that?”

“It’s for self-defense.”

“No, but really, that’s…”

“It’s for self-defense.”

Having that kind of exchange, the two of them pressed forward into the uncharted forest.

With Subaru desperately trying to scrape together whatever resolve he needed to stop the courage he’d just managed to wring out from deflating all over again.
